clue.text: Gaps filled by solid meals

indicators.note: the word for gaps is filled, so it holds the word for solid in its middle

parts.note: breaks are gaps or intervals
fast means firm or solid, as in a fast colour

explanation.surface: Someone plugs holes in their day with hearty, substantial food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solid' looks like an adjective describing the meals, but it is the filling; 'filled by' is the container signal, and 'meals' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning repasts that end the overnight fast are a kind of meal.

clue.text: Bachelor, flexible and happy-go-lucky

parts.note: lithe means supple or flexible

explanation.surface: A single man who is supple and carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a carefree, light-hearted attitude.

clue.text: Fair attribute of party on left

parts.note: to carouse is to party with drink

explanation.surface: A characteristic of a political party that sits on the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' is the fairground, not just; 'party' looks political but is the verb to carouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A merry-go-round is a typical feature of a funfair.

clue.text: Timber and metal where wreck's washed up

parts.note: ash is a hardwood timber
ore is rock from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Wood and iron from a shipwreck end up on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage washed up lies on land, on the beach rather than at sea.

clue.text: Gas — I mean as used to form an oxide

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are used to form a new word by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A chemistry teacher clarifies that a gas reacts to produce an oxide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to form' rearranges GAS I MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnesium oxide is the white powder chemists call by this name.

clue.text: Inadequate short examination

indicators.note: short means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: scant means barely sufficient or inadequate

explanation.surface: A doctor's quick check-up was not thorough enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like an adjective for the examination, but it docks the last letter of SCANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical scan is a kind of close examination.

clue.text: Radical mentioned in diary — Lenin

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: A political extremist is named in a diary entry about Lenin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radical' suggests politics, but in chemistry a radical is a group of atoms, and an aryl group is one; the letters lie in diARY Lenin.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an aryl is a group derived from an aromatic ring, a type of radical.

clue.text: Backing a carriage with girl aboard

indicators.note: aboard means the girl is placed inside the word for carriage

parts.note: carriage means posture or bearing, as does stance
sis is a girl, short for sister

explanation.surface: A girl rides in a horse-drawn coach being pushed from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' suggests a vehicle but means bodily bearing: STANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing means support or help.

clue.text: Fight promoter you might say

parts.note: a scrap is a fight, so a dealer in scrap could be seen as one who sells, or promotes, fights

explanation.surface: Describing a boxing impresario.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrap is also a fight, so a dealer in scrap metal could be read as someone who trades in fights.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in waste metal deals in scrap, and scrap is slang for a fight.

clue.text: Bolt cell back in jail

parts.note: to dart is to bolt or dash

indicators.note: back means the word for cell is turned backwards

parts.note: a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: A prisoner escapes from his cell back into the prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROOM into MOOR. Dartmoor is a well-known prison on the moors of Devon in England.
explanation.definitionFit: HMP Dartmoor is a famous English prison, so the name stands for a jail.

clue.text: College, not the first offering admission

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the college's name is dropped

parts.note: Downing is a college of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A university college, not the top choice, offers a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission' suggests a university place but means confessing; Downing College, Cambridge, loses its first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, so owning means admitting.

clue.text: Those who get commission not in charge of proposals

indicators.note: not means the letters for in charge are left out

parts.note: officers in the armed forces hold a commission

explanation.surface: Salesmen on commission are not responsible for the bids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commission' suggests sales pay but means an officer's warrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Offers are proposals or bids.

clue.text: Force about to indulge in exercises

indicators.note: about means the word for force goes round the word for indulge

parts.note: to press is to force
to sup is to drink, to indulge in liquor

explanation.surface: Being forced to take part in physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: Push-ups on the floor are a standard gym routine.

clue.text: High status with power as head of embassy

indicators.note: as head of means the letter for power is put at the front

parts.note: a residency is the official residence of a diplomat, an embassy

explanation.surface: An ambassador holds a lofty and powerful position.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of a head of state is a position of high rank.

clue.text: Thrust with sword finds bone

parts.note: to shoulder is to thrust or shove
a blade is a sword

explanation.surface: A fencer's lunge discovers a skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: The scapula is a flat bone of the upper back.

clue.text: Alien? The odds are very much against it

definitions.meaning: a foreigner or stranger who does not belong

definitions.text: The odds are very much against it
definitions.meaning: in racing, a long shot unlikely to win

explanation.definitionFit: A stranger who does not belong, and in betting a horse given little chance of winning.

clue.text: Unstrung, the beads found in church

indicators.note: beads that are unstrung come loose and fall into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rosary breaks and the beads are found scattered in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unstrung' rearranges THE BEADS. Bethesda is a name often given to Nonconformist chapels in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a common name for a chapel, a place of worship.

clue.text: Cabbalistic, as coteries can be

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of coteries may be made into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Exclusive cliques often deal in secret mystical lore.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbalistic lore is secret and mystical, understood only by initiates.

clue.text: Dress from Italy — current vogue, in the groove

indicators.note: in means these pieces sit inside the word for groove

parts.note: a rut is a groove worn in a road
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
the go is an old phrase for the fashion, as in all the go

explanation.surface: Italian fashion is stuck in a trendy rut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the groove' sounds like hip slang, but RUT is the groove holding I and GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig-out is an informal word for an outfit of clothes.

clue.text: Barney gets home for lunch

parts.note: a barney is British slang for a quarrel, as is a tiff
in means at home

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when someone comes home for a midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Barney is British slang for a noisy argument. Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian name for a light midday meal.

clue.text: Fellow, shy, in retreat

parts.note: shy means short, as does light, in a pound light

explanation.surface: A timid man hides himself away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like timid but means short of, as LIGHT does.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight is running away, a retreat from danger.

clue.text: Smart grabbing rook file

indicators.note: grabbing means the word for smart holds the letter for rook

parts.note: to smart is to sting
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A clever operator seizes a rook from the chessboard's file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'file' suggests a chess file but means a line, as a string of people is.
explanation.definitionFit: A file of people in a line is a string of them.

clue.text: Add up and carry

definitions.meaning: to total figures, as in tot up

explanation.definitionFit: Totting figures together sums them, and lugging a load is carrying it.

clue.text: Fishes I have in Wales, battered

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A fish-and-chip shop in Wales fries fish in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' suggests the chip shop but rearranges I'VE and WALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Alewives are North American fish of the herring family.

clue.text: A vocal number, a duet unusually rarefied

indicators.note: vocal means the words are said aloud and spelt as they sound

parts.note: ten is a number; said straight after the opening A, a ten runs together as one sound

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of a duet are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A vocal piece for two singers is strangely refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vocal' looks like it describes the song, but says A TEN aloud, heard as ATTEN; 'unusually' rearranges A DUET into UATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Attenuated means thinned out, as rarefied air is thin.

clue.text: Pledge with wine

definitions.meaning: to pawn something as security for a loan
a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.definitionFit: To pawn an item is to leave it as security, and German Rhine whites carry the name in Britain.
